note: SDBD double byte data (pdf 47; Fig 3.2.6 and 3.2.7, pdf 49; pdf 57, 58) and the refusal of every other target (POL-SDBD-02). Every vector starts with the SDBD word $0001 and runs the SDBD unit and its target as two steps. Every expect value is read from the cited page image and derived by hand; none comes from this core, an assembler or another implementation. The double byte READ offsets are inference (C36): no figure prints them.

vectors.cite: Immediate double byte data table, MVII row, pdf 58; SDBD row, pdf 57; Fig 3.2.7, pdf 49; S3.2.1 double byte data, pdf 47; C34
vectors.derivation: Two units. Step 1, SDBD (0000 000 001, pdf 57, 4 cycles) sets DBD for the next instruction. Step 2, MVII I, DDD: the immediate double byte table (pdf 58) prints 1010 111 DDD with DDD = 001 (R1) after the SDBD word, then XXLL LLL LLL and XXUU UUU UUU (XX = don't care; Fig 3.2.7, pdf 49: bits 15..8 'Not Used'), 'L's will be low byte and U's upper byte'. Fig 3.2.7: EA_L <- (PC+1), EA_H <- (PC+2), PC <- PC+3, so R7 goes $1000 -> $1001 (SDBD) -> $1004. pdf 47: the low data byte is the low 8 bits of the first word and the high byte the low 8 bits of the second, so the operand is ($AB34 AND $00FF) = $34 low and ($CD12 AND $00FF) = $12 high, $1234; bits 15..8 of both words ($AB, $CD) take no part. MVII: 'MoVe In Immediate double byte data to register DDD', no status change: R1 = $1234 and the flags keep their initial 0. Cycles: the SDBD unit is 4 (pdf 57) and the target prints 14 including the SDBD word (pdf 58), i.e. 10 for the instruction unit, so the two units take 4 + 10 = 14 (C34, A-05). SDBD is non-interruptible by the C56 default and the target row has no Not Interruptable note, so prev_interruptible ends 1. DBD is set by the SDBD unit and cleared by the target that consumes it, so it ends 0. Bus (inference, C36: no figure prints a double byte access): FETCH of the SDBD word at cycle 0 (pdf 28), FETCH of the target at cycle 4 (the SDBD unit is its printed 4 cycles), the low byte READ at 4 + 4 = 8 (the data access BAR of pdf 29) and the high byte READ at 4 + 7 = 11 (the second read takes the place of the trailing NACT of the 8-cycle read, so the 10-cycle unit ends after its data transfer). Registers and memory not named stay unchanged.

Fig 3.2.6 (pdf 49), MMM = 1, 2, 3: PC <- PC+1, EA_L <- (MMM), EA_H <- (MMM), no register change; the SDBD row (pdf 57) says modes 1-3 'will access the same byte twice resulting in both bytes of data being the same'. pdf 47 says only one word is accessed; POL-SDBD-01 as amended by A-03 (C37, policy) takes two READs of the same address. pdf 47: the low data byte is the low 8 bits of the first word read and the high byte the low 8 bits of the second, so the operand is $01 low and $01 high, both from the word $7701 at $0300, $0101. R7 goes $1000 -> $1001 -> $1002. ADD@ adds it to R3, status S, Z, C, OV (pdf 57): $0001 + $0101 = $0102 with no carry out and no sign change (pdf 45), so R3 = $0102 and S = Z = OV = C = 0, clearing their initial 1. R2 stays $0300. Cycles: the SDBD unit is 4 (pdf 57) and the target row prints 10 under the separate 4-cycle SDBD row (pdf 57), so the two units take 4 + 10 = 14 (C34, A-05). SDBD is non-interruptible by the C56 default and the target row has no Not Interruptable note, so prev_interruptible ends 1. DBD is set by the SDBD unit and cleared by the target that consumes it, so it ends 0. Bus (inference, C36: no figure prints a double byte access): FETCH of the SDBD word at cycle 0 (pdf 28), FETCH of the target at cycle 4 (the SDBD unit is its printed 4 cycles), the low byte READ at 4 + 4 = 8 (the data access BAR of pdf 29) and the high byte READ at 4 + 7 = 11 (the second read takes the place of the trailing NACT of the 8-cycle read, so the 10-cycle unit ends after its data transfer). Registers and memory not named stay unchanged.
